choices.where: the PR as a whole: eight declarations in seven files
choices.pr_choice: Batches eight unrelated proofs from seven files across order theory, finsets, rationals, measure theory, probability and metric spaces into one PR.
choices.visibility_reason: A proof-only task cannot be stated without naming the declarations whose proofs change; the files are also visible as packet: base files.
choices.consequence: A different batch (fewer files, one area per PR) changes how many reviewers from different areas a single PR needs and how easily it can be split or merged.

choices.pr_choice: Changes only proofs; every statement, name and hypothesis is left as at the base.
choices.status_reason: The goal is a golf of existing results; the statements and their uses must keep working.
choices.visibility_reason: Stated in section 3 as a preservation requirement.
choices.consequence: Changing a statement would break downstream uses and turn a golf into an API change.

choices.pr_choice: Frames the golf as using `grind` and `simp` throughout.
choices.consequence: Committing to particular automation affects elaboration time and how proofs react to future changes in that automation or the simp set.

choices.pr_choice: Replaces the explicit anonymous-constructor proof with a `simp only` unfolding followed by `grind`.
choices.consequence: Brings `grind` into a low-level finset file and, per the description, raises this lemma's elaboration time from under 10 ms to 25 ms; the proof now depends on grind's behaviour.

choices.pr_choice: Replaces the rewrite chain through `divInt` and coprimality with a `simp only` using the inverse-denominator and integer-cast numerator lemmas, then `grind`.
choices.consequence: Per the description, elaboration time rises from under 10 ms to 17 ms; the proof depends on grind closing a goal about integer signs and absolute values.

choices.pr_choice: Replaces the final product reindexing via `Finset.prod_equiv` and `congr` with `simp only [pi_pi, this]` and a term using `Fintype.prod_equiv`.
Golfs only the tail of these proofs, keeping the opening `let`/`have` blocks (the preimage computation and the disintegration rewrite) as they were.

Instead of going through the primed ENNReal criterion with a bottom-filter case split and finiteness side goals, rewrites the hypothesis with `ProbabilityMeasure.measureReal_eq_coe_coeFn` and `NNReal.toReal_limsup` and applies the unprimed criterion directly.
choices.consequence: Per the description, elaboration drops from 268 ms to under 10 ms; the lemma now depends on the unprimed criterion and on `NNReal.toReal_limsup` rather than the ENNReal route, so changes there propagate here.

choices.pr_choice: Replaces the explicit witness set ⋂ i ∈ s, {a | F i a < b} with a `simp only` through `sup'_lt_iff` and `eventually_all_finset` at the hypothesis and goal, then a one-line term.
choices.excerpt: simp only [gt_iff_lt, sup'_lt_iff, eventually_all_finset] at hb ⊢

choices.pr_choice: Replaces the `compProd_apply` plus indicator-function computation (with `classical` and a case split) by `simp only [this]` and the product-set lemma `compProd_apply_prod` / `Kernel.compProd_apply_prod`, applied identically in both versions.

Turns the tactic proof with an explicit midpoint and `linarith` into a term-mode proof by the order lemma `exists_between'`, relying on ball membership unfolding definitionally to a distance inequality.
choices.consequence: Per the description, elaboration drops from 81 ms to under 10 ms; the proof depends on the definitional unfolding of `x ∈ ball y ε`, so it would break if `ball` were redefined.

choices.pr_choice: Includes two rewrites that the PR's own profiling shows elaborating slower than the base proofs, trading time for brevity.
choices.consequence: A golf that slows elaboration adds build time; a designer under a no-slowdown reading would drop or redo these two.

feasibility_reason: The task is a golf of named existing declarations whose statements, names and files are base facts. Only the set of declarations (and so the files) must be exposed, because a proof-only task cannot be stated otherwise. Every consequential proposed choice is a proof route or a trade-off (grind in low-level files, the Portmanteau reduction to the unprimed criterion, the definitional term proof of the ball lemma, accepting two slowdowns, how much of each proof to rewrite) and all of them are withheld.
brief_omits: The tactics named in the title (grind, simp); every lemma the new proofs use; the profiling figures, including the base ones, since with the description's inclusion rule a '<10 ms before' entry reveals a slowdown; the numeric batch limits (about 5 files, 25 declarations, 100 lines), paraphrased as 'size guidelines' to avoid quoting the description's scope statement; that some proofs keep their opening let/have blocks; that one proof becomes term-mode.
